# V13 collection-only arbitration: completed Amin histories

After all12 selected games completed, the four Amin games show V10 winning both cases1/2 at1033 and V13 losing both at519. The cases are opposite seats/spawn labels on one consumed83000 placement, not independent maps. All3,104 original candidate frames were reduced, with exact role-relative mirror equality for public wires, raw/applied actions, validity, original19-field memory and telemetry. No new inference, engine replay or games were used.

| Policy | Case | Result / turns | Candidate invalid / malformed | Original Amin invalid / malformed |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|
| V10 |1|win /1033|0/0|58/0|
| V10 |2|win /1033|0/0|58/0|
| V13 |1|loss /519|0/0|12/0|
| V13 |2|loss /519|0/0|12/0|

All140 original opponent invalids remain normalized in the evidence; they are not infrastructure/deadline faults. V13's invalid-opponent turns per case are77,103,106,149,152,227,230,263,318,359,368,474. None occurs during the final visible invasion505–518. Synchronous adapter results do not qualify deployment deadlines. Original policy recording includes IO in timings.

## First veto is transient, not a sufficient terminal explanation

The first candidate raw/applied difference is193, first differing public observations194, and first opponent raw/applied difference281. At193 the public input, incoming memory and key match V10. V13 replaces the original recorded collection proposal `(16,12)→(16,13)` toward enemy(15,15) with immediate capture `(7,9)8→(6,9)enemy1`, leaving6. It starts the original collection at194 and captures its objective at197, one turn after V10's196.

Crucially, both players' public observations and the candidate's incoming19-field memory and key **rejoin exactly at198 and remain equal through219**; joint raw actions are identical198–218. This does not certify every hidden engine/opponent internal field, but it rules out describing the first veto as permanent abandonment of that objective or treating its initial divergence as a sufficient explanation of the later defeat. A second veto219 again occurs on matching public input/memory; its original collection starts220 and captures223.

## Actual allocation changes and preserved deployments

Each V13 game issues11 collection-capture overrides:193,219,300,301,320–323,414,415,510. Every one is an actually legal enemy-plain capture, confirmed owned in the next public observation. Every rejected original parent proposal is archived as five scalar action fields; every replacement has `offense_started && offense_collecting`, and unissued offense memory clears. There are no rejected direct deployments. Actual start counts after all outer issuance masks are29 collection and40 direct starts; the longer1033-turn V10 controls contain47/95, so those raw totals are not comparable strength rates. Both versions have only the same12 opening PASS turns; V13 builds once at381.

Direct deployment is preserved in actual behavior, including the original163 three-action attack. Later V13 starts a nine-action direct route at287 from army17 at(14,17), captures(8,14) on295 and has17 there at296. An eight-action direct route starts310 from army16 at(9,17), captures(15,15) on317 and has17 there at318. These examples demonstrate that the collection-only rule does not reproduce V11's direct-start veto mechanically; they do not establish adequate whole-game offense.

Repeated reselection still creates capture-versus-assembly tradeoffs. At300–301, two immediate captures consume a10-army packet down to4 while delaying the same six-action assembly toward(14,16), which starts302. At320–323, four enemy2 captures take army14 at(15,14) west to(15,10), leaving2: eight enemy defenders plus four departure garrisons explain the moving force reduction. The proposed remote six-action assembly toward(7,7) is repeatedly deferred, starts324 and captures329. At414–415 two captures delay another collection, which starts416 and captures419. These are real territorial gains and finite delays, not proof the rejected objectives were worthless or permanently abandoned. The new trajectory has eleven actual triggers, distinct from the twelve hypothetical triggers previously counted on the old V10 history.

## Force, economy and terminal loss

The candidate is not simply losing every economy comparison. At324 it leads land88–72 and army287–262; by414 it trails land78–97 and army341–359. At500 it again leads land108–89 and army484–464. At518 it has army446 versus417 despite land98–100. Local force concentration and action timing remain decisive.

The final large enemy stack is visible at(8,5)152 on505, then(7,5)157, (7,6)154, (7,7)151, (7,8)148, (7,9)146, (7,10)143, (7,11)140, then east along row8. Home has40 on509. There is no active DefenderMemory or feasible interception certificate throughout509–518. Nevertheless the ordinary campaign issues several local moves:

1. At509 it sends half of home down: home21 and army24 at(9,17) on510. The last collection veto510 instead sends army20 at(6,9) left to capture enemy5; the proposed collection starts511.
2. At513 it returns the24-army packet into home, yielding46 at514. At514 it sends half left, yielding army25 at(8,16) and home23 at515.
3. At515 that screen moves down to(9,16), then returns up516; at517 it attempts to return from(8,16)27 into home. Simultaneously enemy125 at(8,15) attacks its source.
4. The frozen engine resolves chasing before reinforcing (`generals/core/game.py::_determine_move_order`), then checks source ownership when executing each move. Enemy capture resolves first: the screen becomes enemy97 and its outgoing reinforcement cannot execute. Public518 shows home25, only its growth increment, rather than receiving the intended26-army transfer. Enemy97 captures home at519.

Both517 commands are valid against the initial public state and retained as applied commands. This is a gameplay move-order/source-capture failure, not a malformed command, runner normalization error or evidence that the recorded policy action was different. The joint actions, public observations and original memory are embedded in the machine report; the explanation follows the frozen engine source without running a counterfactual transition.

This exposes an inherited reactive local-movement failure while the defender module cannot certify a solution. It does not prove a rescue existed under an alternative policy or quantify the causal contribution of each earlier collection veto. The final four-step local loop is ordinary campaign behavior with inactive DefenderMemory, unlike attributing every such loop to commitment expiry. Earlier global allocation and later tactical handling must remain distinct hypotheses.

## Evidence and conclusion

`analysis.json` retains all outcomes, invalid lists, original parent/issued replacement actions and telemetry, masked start counts, exact mirror/rejoin checks and terminal public evidence. `timeline.jsonl` reduces all3,104 original candidate frames. `postchecks.json` verifies exact historical V10 wires/actions/outcomes and original memory/key/telemetry parity. `delivery-manifest.json` binds these reports, source freeze, completed run and every input hash; all immutable inputs were rechecked after analysis. The first analysis attempt passed. Frozen prior reports, policy sources and game artifacts remain unchanged.

The fixed collection-only ablation fails Amin preservation on this placement even though it preserves actual ready deployments. That rejects the preservation hypothesis here; it does not establish that every immediate capture is bad or that the first veto caused the loss. No promotion, default change, fresh-map claim or broad competitive superiority follows.

## my_bot9: earlier ordinary general capture, with defense retained

The first candidate difference is100; the first opponent difference106. At100 the rule replaces a five-action proposed collection with4 attacking enemy2 at(7,6), leaving1 next frame. This tile remains owned200 observations. At150 another replacement captures enemy2 at(1,3) with1 survivor, retained333 observations through the terminal state (right-censored). These are the only two substitutions.

The adaptive trajectory develops an advantage: at200 own54land/151army versus26/85, and at35056/235 versus45/190. It builds once at415. Later it temporarily yields ground to an enemy packet, but the inherited defender remains available: at472–474 it transfers its selected defender down an owned route while the estimated home deficit drops12→8→4. The plan releases475 when deficit0; this is not a V13 override or a claimed counterfactual rescue.

The attack packet proceeds across row7 and then north at columns12/13. The enemy general is first publicly visible481, much earlier than the control's late-game discovery. At482 own21 at(4,13) sends20 into the visible enemy general19 at(4,14), winning at483 through ordinary combat. Own home remains33. All final actions retain the parent output, with no remembered-target pursuit override and no V10 deathtouch mobilization in this game. The one-substitution explanation is insufficient: the opponent responds adaptively and the policy continues making hundreds of different choices afterward.

## Bounded next discrimination and limits

The useful next question is the earlier campaign allocation conflict, not another blanket capture veto: on the already retained common opening100–128, compare the action cost and delivered force of the existing large packet's ongoing useful route with the small new collection, while retaining the successful Amin collection193/292 and ready-direct controls. A prospective test would need to specify when an existing campaign packet deserves continuity and preserve defense, structural goals, and winning captures. This report proposes no tuned threshold and claims no rescue or improvement from such a change.

All parent offensive/defense event counts are masked by the actual V13 parent-action flag and the inherited mobilization/actual-V8 masks as applicable. Unissued proposal fields are not counted as executed plans. Captures/retention require next saved ownership; current policy inputs are public wires only. Complete saved engine state is used for evidence validation, not policy inference. No new policy or engine inference, matches, or source edits occurred in this diagnosis.

Its helper/log are retained; r2 fixes only that schema access. r3 additionally exports the final public source/destination force and late feasibility/mask fields. # J35 opening concentration versus V6's winning campaign

This is a cache-only audit, without new policy/engine inference or games. It binds the complete archived V6 win1075 and V9 loss422, verifies their label-mirror raw histories, and verifies that **all422 public wires, applied actions and candidate incoming/returned memory** in the V9 diagnostic agree with the freshly completed V12 selected **V10 control**. Archived same-observation V6 proposal telemetry can therefore be used on the current frozen V10 loss without inventing a new observation. The full51-frame opening action table, actual subsequent captures and economy counts are in report.json. The old state reconstruction is derived from the exact original engine/actions; it is not an independently archived intermediate-state oracle.

## Earliest strategic divergence has a real opportunity cost

First candidate action difference is100; first opponent raw-action difference is116. At100 both policies see36land/86army against38/90. V6 moves the8 at(9,17) into(10,17), then follows eight owned transfers in total, absorbing real garrisons and reaching16 at(11,11) on108. It captures enemy(11,10) at108, then takes seven tiles at108–115 (six enemy, one neutral), with one interleaved home expansion. The same packet follows through instead of stopping after one affordable target.

V10 instead begins a five-action collection100–104 using the3 at(14,12), predicted delivery6/requirement6 for enemy target(11,10). It really captures that tile104, four turns sooner, and holds it for22 observations. At105 it takes a second enemy tile with the small remainder. At106 it begins another five-action collection toward enemy(12,10), delivery4/requirement4; it captures110 and holds67 observations. These are useful actual captures, so a rule that labels all such plans wasted would be wrong.

The cost appears in **what happens next**. V10 finally performs the exact same eight-move large-packet route at115–122,15turns after V6; the second weak collection also uses some cells from the first route, reducing available follow-through. Through110 both branches spent eight owned transfers and captured three tiles. But through123 V6 spent nine owned transfers and captured15 tiles, while V10 spent17 transfers and captured7. Through149 V6 has27 actual captures (11 enemy,16 neutral), versus V10's17 (13 enemy,4 neutral). At150 this becomes55land/142army for V6 versus42/118 for V10. V10 captures more enemy tiles in this opening window while developing substantially less total land. Cheap single-target delivery and enemy affiliation alone therefore miss a measurable campaign tradeoff.

This establishes actual early allocation/tempo differences, not that forcing the V6 move100 alone wins. Later opposing actions adapt and diverge116. Neither branch builds a castle before422, so lost castle opportunities cannot explain this early gap. Nor is the final threat already visible: the terminal army is first observed415, long after the economy split.

## The129 case is a later, distinct instance

At129 the already-diverged winning V6 branch spends its next five moves capturing empty neutral cells from small independent donors. The losing V10 branch begins an eight-action collection toward enemy1 at(11,10), taking seven owned transfers and one capture136. Its immediate V6 proposal **on that same V10 observation** is a different opportunity: capture enemy1 at(7,8) from own5 at(8,8). That immediate enemy capture is what V11/V13 arbitration targets; it must not be confused with the actual V6 branch's neutral expansion sequence.

The129 collection's target remains owned for only six observations. The immediate source's affordable enemy capture remains available in the archived V10 observations129–135, then reinforcement closes it. V11's actual adaptive substitution129 did improve local capture tempo and prolong this selected Juraj loss, but still lost887. It also damaged Amin elsewhere. The existing studies do not prove that any broad capture veto recovers V6's overall strength.

## Collection-only V11 ablation: testable, with clear limits

Restricting arbitration to a **new collection**, leaving ready direct deployment and ongoing plans alone, is a bounded structural experiment. It keeps the J35 collection129 intervention and avoids V11's first harmful Amin direct-deployment diversion163. The first J35 differences100/106 remain untouched because the V6 reference action then is an owned transfer, not an immediate enemy capture. Therefore success cannot be assumed to recover V6's earliest campaign behavior; the candidate only addresses one later class of interruption.

The preservation risk is concrete. On the successful original Amin game1 trajectory, collection-only arbitration would still reject12 starts. The first is193: four actions capture enemy1 at(15,15) on196 with5 survivors, held63 observations, while the V6 alternative is a different immediate enemy1 capture from8army at(7,9) into(6,9). Collection292 takes six actions and retains its enemy1 target56 observations. Training's complete census finds11 of the12 collections actually capture their objectives, all11 held at least25 observations (some end-censored); one aborts. These are counterexamples to declaring the masked collections worthless, not proof that their replacement necessarily loses. The earlier useful Amin collections129/142 are also preserved by the proposed immediate-enemy gate, but preserving just those two is insufficient evidence.

The next discriminating experiment is the preregistered full adaptive12-game comparison, without weakening success criteria or choosing a mode from the results. If collection-only still harms Amin or fails to recover Juraj, the opening evidence suggests a separate later hypothesis: compare the campaign value of an existing packet's multi-capture continuation with a minimum-sufficient one-target assembly, instead of only comparing target defending armies or first-capture ETA. Such a policy would need public route/force feasibility and strong negative controls; no implementation or efficacy claim is made here.

No143000 data was inspected. Original sources, archives and prior artifacts remain unchanged. All numerical tables and counterexamples are source/hash bound in report.json and bindings.json.

campaign_controls_report:
# Campaign controls for a collection-only ablation

This read-only audit uses complete original V10 Amin cases1/2 from the V12 cycle, with exact historical control parity, plus the earlier complete same-observation V6 proposal audit and V11/V12 recorded failures. No new games, policy inference, threshold tuning or reserved143000 data were used. Cases1/2 are one mirrored consumed placement, not independent maps.

## Concrete distinctions available at decision time

**Assembly is not ready deployment.** In `generals/agents/sentinel_v8_agent.py`, `offense_started` plus `offense_collecting` means a new owned-route assembly, while `offense_direct_chosen` means deployment of an already sufficient packet. `offense_remaining` is the current phase's distance, not the whole plan budget; use `offense_collection_eta` for a new assembly's collection-plus-deployment budget. The earliest productive Amin129 plan has two collection and two deployment actions, with no direct packet available for its chosen objective;142 has six collection plus two deployment. Both actually capture and remain owned43/25 observations. Army/land deficit, a four-action cap, or a generic available immediate capture fails to separate them from distraction.

**Actual issuance matters.** An original V10 offensive start is attributable to the action only when the inherited `offense_started` is accompanied by `actual_v8_action_issued` and `mobilization_parent_action_issued`; outer wrappers require their own parent-issued mask. `offense_home_coverage_safe` is a modeled local resistance condition, not a claim that a defender plan is executing or that home can survive every future enemy move. V12t249 has no commitment start/continue/hold, intercept override, offensive start/continue/override or pursuit issuance. It is an ordinary campaign transfer from army12 at(8,15) to owned1 at(8,14), observed13 after transfer/growth. The V12 route guard rejected that move, not a claimed defensive interception. At V12t495 a parent defender-start flag exists but its action is replaced and memory cleared; that flag is not an executed start.

**A legal capture is not strategic dominance over another location.** The old V11 comparison checks immediate enemy-plain capture against a newly selected enemy-plain objective with no greater defending army. That compares current legal combat and target type, not the objectives' future access or ownership value. V6's alternative uses the actual current incoming defender memory in the earlier verified proposal audit; it is not an independently evolved counterfactual policy history.

## Exact positive and negative controls

- **129/142 productive assembly:** preserve the distinction between assembling small owned garrisons and moving a large ready packet. At129 the route combines three2-army garrisons to4, then captures enemy(14,10)1 at132. The base could instead spend a22-army packet capturing neutral land. The original game alone cannot prove the collection caused its eventual win.
- **163 ready-direct negative control for the proposed veto:** army15 at(9,9) has a three-action route to enemy(12,9)2, captured on action165 with12 survivors. V11's actual immediate captures instead sent that packet north twice before backtracking and defensive interruption. Later V11 direct-capture chains327–331 and402–408 consume/divert ready force. A NEW COLLECTION-only rule must leave163 unchanged even though its ETA exceeds1 and another enemy capture is legal. Fixtures embed the exact original public wire,19-field incoming memory, key and V10 action `[0,9,9,1,0]` for both mirrors.
- **193 productive-collection counterexample:** this is the first collection-only trigger on the unchanged successful control history. The route is `(16,12)3→(16,13)3→(16,14)2→(16,15)2→enemy(15,15)1`. Two assembly actions produce5 then6; deployment picks up a further garrison and captures at196 with5 survivors. The objective remains owned63 following observations. The alternative is a legal immediate enemy1 capture from(7,9)8 to(6,9), leaving6. These are different fronts. The proposed rule intentionally rejects the original productive four-action assembly; neither equal target defenders nor greater immediate survivors proves that rejection improves the full game. Exact original fixtures include action `[0,16,12,3,0]`, key/memory and separately sourced V6 proposal.
- **292 further counterexample:** six-action assembly to(11,14)1 captures at297 with5 survivors, retained56 observations. A direct route to the same selected objective is available but costs7 actions, so choosing collection is not simply ignoring a faster ready route. The V6 immediate alternative captures a different enemy1 from a30-army packet. Restricting to collection still changes this productive plan.
- **506 aborted assembly, not proof of foolish admission:** the selected five-action assembly spends four actions and then releases at510 for defensive priority. This is the sole uncaptured objective among the12 common-history collection triggers. A later necessary interruption does not demonstrate that the initial public-state choice was already dominated. Future capture/retention is diagnostic evidence, never an online admission feature.

## Proposed falsifiable experiment and limits

The precise ablation is the old V11 immediate-enemy-capture preference intersected with **new, actually issued collection**: `offense_started && offense_collecting`, outer parent-issued masks, legal V6 enemy-plain capture, selected enemy-plain objective no more defended than the immediate target, and the unchanged multi-action condition. Preserve existing continuations, ready direct deployment, structures/general pursuit and defensive/winning priority behavior; keep the same reference V6 call and unissued-memory reconciliation. This changes the strategic allocation of a turn from starting assembly toward attacking an existing front. It is more specific than narrowing a generic route guard, and introduces no outcome-chosen ETA threshold.

On the unchanged successful history it triggers12 starts per mirror:193,219,292,300,314,324,404,501,506,790,832,886. Eleven actually capture their objectives, all11 retained at least25 observations, including one end-censored hold. These are opportunity-cost hazards, not12 proof-of-error labels. Only the first trigger can be treated as the prospective common-prefix decision; after193 an adaptive opponent and candidate memory create a new trajectory. Do not predict the new run will necessarily visit the remaining11 triggers.

There is no decisive correctness reason not to test this fixed ablation. There is decisive evidence against claiming it preserves all productive collection or must preserve the Amin win. The necessary discrimination is complete adaptive outcomes plus issued plan/capture/continuation attribution on both the original successful Amin case and the Juraj failure, retaining all failures and invalid actions. If direct deployments are preserved yet Amin still regresses, the explanation cannot remain solely V11's ready-packet detours; the allocation between remote assembly and immediate capture must be assessed directly. Full12-case testing is warranted before broader claims, and the broader six-opponent goal remains unresolved.

## Artifacts

`amin-game-000{1,2}-turn-0163.json` and `...0193.json` contain the original recorded inputs, expected V10 action, returned memory and telemetry, observed objective outcomes and provenance. `fixture-manifest.json` binds immutable source/run inputs and all four fixture hashes. `evidence.json` retains all12 collection-trigger rows, explicit criteria and source/report hashes. No policy import or inference was needed. The first exploratory JSON query encountered a null capture record; it was corrected to treat a released plan as lacking a capture, rather than dropping the row.

# V13 architecture audit

Read-only source and completed-development evidence; no policy inference, games, or reserved-seed use.

## Final action and memory chain

V6 calls V5, which uses the frozen V2 campaign scores plus interception. V6 can continue a committed defender or hold it by selecting another campaign move; immediate general capture retains priority (`sentinel_v6_agent.py:174–175`). This is a measured stronger control on some opponents, not a certified defense oracle: the later donation/alternate-route counterexamples still apply.

V8 calls V6 exactly once (`sentinel_v8_agent.py:70`). A feasible, home-screen-safe collection/deployment replaces the result without comparing its action cost or reward with the campaign choice (187–208). Incoming/returned defender state, guard, adjacent threat, reserve deficit and immediate general win block this replacement. Actual builds block *new* plans; continuing plans can replace builds and ordinary captures. Expected arrival force, continuity, remaining distance and fixed expiry constrain continuation. V8 keeps the returned V6 defense and updates its own eight transport fields, for fifteen scalar memory leaves.

V9 always constructs V8 with both features (55); a known but currently hidden stationary enemy-general coordinate can direct pursuit. It does not fabricate occupancy or armies. Priority excludes V8 defense, positive interception deficit, commitment events, actual builds and a currently visible enemy general (137–147). A changed pursuit action clears unissued offense transport, retains returned defense and stationary knowledge (149–155). There are nineteen scalar leaves. `pursuit_issued` includes same-action agreement; `pursuit_override` is the actual action change. `actual_v8_action_issued` masks inherited proposals; `pursuit_base_*` records the actual V8 proposal (167–174).

V10 chooses V9 or V6 statically (27–36), invokes it once, and conditionally substitutes a home-sourced interception after deathtouch. Its eligibility excludes existing defenders and adjacent/guard emergencies; the proposed source must improve ETA/force and preserve its current home-route check. A changed action clears both transport memories in the nineteen-leaf parent, preserving stationary knowledge; parent6 uses seven leaves (118–127). `mobilization_parent_action_issued` is the outer inherited-event mask. Its certificate does not repair all V5/V6 route-accounting defects.

For final V10default telemetry, V8 issued events require both `actual_v8_action_issued` and `mobilization_parent_action_issued`; V9 pursuit requires the latter. Do not count a proposal as executed merely because the inherited event is true. V11/V12/V13 add an additional outer mask. `building` is usually rewritten to the selected action, while most inherited counters remain proposals.

## What the existing controls isolate

| Configuration | Actual delegation / retained mechanisms |
|---|---|
| V6 disabled | V5, no continued-defense memory behavior |
| V7 disabled / no concentration | V6 with wrapper memory |
| V8 cheap | Cheap collection; no ready-direct shortcut |

No existing control isolates **V6 plus remembered-general pursuit**, nor direct deployment with collection entirely disabled. The former is a small, meaningful next factorial alternative after the currently selected V13 experiment: retain the verified stationary-goal behavior over the stronger local commander without new economy/defense rules. It is not guaranteed to preserve Amin gains. Simply assigning a disabled-concentration V8 base inside V9 is insufficient: the delegated telemetry lacks `offense_defense_priority`; a candidate-owned explicit adapter and exact disabled-parent contract are required.

V13 is a narrower V11 structural ablation: only *new collecting* starts can lose priority to an immediate ordinary enemy capture of at least the objective's current defenders. Ready direct deployment, continued plans and structures retain parent priority. It instruments the owned V8-to-V6 call via frozen V11 `_ReferenceAction`, avoiding another policy solve. Clearing only unissued offense while retaining returned defense and general knowledge matches that replacement. Disabled mode delegates exactly V10. The new five `collection_parent_*` fields retain the actual outer parent action; all inherited events need `collection_capture_parent_action_issued`. No implementation blocker found in the reviewed source. This is a hypothesis, not a proof: actual Amin163 direct is preserved, while actual Amin193 productive collection is deliberately overridden.

## Completed evidence constrains the next hypothesis

The V8 stage-one arms show non-additivity: Amin scores V6 46.875%, V7 43.75%, cheap31.25%, direct40.625%, both62.5%; Hunter V6 100%, V7/direct/both87.5%, cheap93.75%. No isolated feature preserved every control. V9's fixed432 games raised Amin from V8 20W12L to22W10L and Hunter28W4L to30W2L, while remaining below V6's32W Hunter. Its late seen-general Hunter pair improved; the never-seen-general early loss remained. All sixteen J35 V8/V9 histories matched, so remembered-general pursuit cannot explain those regressions. V10's parent6 aggregate matched V6 over all six opponents in the576-game gate; it removes two mechanisms together and is not the missing factorial.

The complete V8 Amin same-observation audit found 3,286 replaced visible capture proposals and56 replaced legal builds, but also a productive collection counterexample; counts alone do not establish harmful opportunity cost. V11's unrestricted capture arbitration then lost the selected Amin control after changing ready deployment. V13 preserves that direct branch but can still suppress productive collection. Opponent entropy and mirrored samples must remain qualified; none of these consumed development histories supports universal strength or promotion.

## Instrumentation and performance boundaries

V8 does not expose the generic V6 proposal vector; V11's one-call wrapper is a cheap way to do so. V9 exposes V8 proposals, while frozen V10 does not archive every preceding generic action. Record each arbitration input/output vector, actual change and outer issued masks before claiming which layer caused an action. Keep source/key/full incoming memory and reset reasons. Full source replay is not an independent proof of the policy's memory logic. Some older local runs lack full traces; reconstructed public wires must be labelled as such.

A static base selection may remove graph work, but no speedup is established by this read-only audit. Avoid executing V6 and V8 separately just to expose the same internal action. Current planning has multiple spatial distance fields; expanding all source-target alternatives could dominate runtime. New static class/options/telemetry signatures require new source/archive/cache qualification: prior compiled artifacts cannot certify a new first-call limit. Matched fixed-state CPU/GPU throughput is a bounded gate, not worst-case full-episode latency. Cold JAX compilation in recent variants exceeds the10-second first-reply allowance without supported cache prewarming.
